category_title: Student with ASD and intellectual disabilities who relies on visual modeling and struggles with multiplicative vocabulary
student_description: Peter is a 14-year-old student with ASD and intellectual disabilities who relies heavily on drawing to solve math problems but struggles with language comprehension, often misinterpreting multiplicative vocabulary as additive or literal text. He uniquely needs complex vocabulary simplified (e.g., 'double' instead of 'times as many') and his informal drawings (like arrows connecting sets) explicitly bridged to structured conceptual model diagrams.

criteria.rationale: Peter's language comprehension deficits cause him to use the wrong operations, requiring explicit instruction on how specific phrases map to sections of a model diagram.
criteria.check: The tutor's plan includes explicitly teaching specific math vocabulary (e.g., 'distributed equally', 'the one with more') and directly aligning those terms with corresponding sections in a conceptual model diagram.

criteria.criterion_name: Bridging Informal Drawings to Formal Operations
criteria.rationale: Peter naturally relies on trial-and-error drawing; connecting these drawings to formal model diagrams bridges his visual preference to actual mathematical operations.
criteria.check: The tutor's plan systematically connects the student's visual representations (e.g., arrows, drawings) to formal model diagrams (e.g., by underlining words below boxes or linking arrows to the 'total combinations' expression).
